Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of review:** Against Buyer Playbook; no authority instructions received for any fallback position.

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing is not to be accepted

The Seller's preamble asserts that its positions (i) are "standard and widely accepted market terms", (ii) were "settled at principal level by both deal teams", and (iii) are "marked FINAL and not intended to be re-opened".

**None of this should be treated as true for our purposes.** Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, a counterparty assertion that something is "market", "agreed" or "final" has no effect on our positions unless confirmed through our own authority process. We have no record of any principal-level agreement on these terms, and nothing from Amelia Frost authorising any fallback. Note in particular that the Seller's cap (20% / AUD 4.8m) and claims period (18 months) happen to match exactly our *conditional* fallbacks – that is not a coincidence we should reward. A number matching a fallback does not clear it; the fallback is only usable with prior written authority identifying the draft, and none exists. **Recommendation: respond on the basis that the Seller's draft is an opening position, and ask the Seller to identify the basis for the "settled at principal level" statement.**

The Disclosure Letter's own para 11 ("No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included") actually contradicts the cover note's claim that positions are agreed – worth pointing out.

---

## 1. Clause-by-clause departures

### 1.1 Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 opening; 20% is fallback-only with Amelia Frost written approval (not given).
- **Push back:** Hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal that 20% is acceptable. If the deal team wants to move, that is a decision for Amelia Frost to document first.

### 1.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Analysis:** Three separate degradations – the de minimis is 5x ours, the basket 5x ours, and the basket is converted from a tipping basket to a deductible. On a AUD 24m SaaS target, a AUD 25k de minimis would exclude a large proportion of realistic operational claims (e.g. individual customer/supplier issues, employee entitlement errors). The "1% basket is market" assertion in the preamble is just an assertion.
- **Push back:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket. This is a material economic point, not drafting.

### 1.3 Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and the "all Claims" catch-all
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is fallback-only with Amelia Frost approval (not given). Fundamental/Title at least six years; Tax/IP open and separate.
- **Analysis:** The 18 months is the same fallback-matching tactic as the cap. The second sentence is the more dangerous one: it is a **hidden general-regime override**. Combined with the Seller's Fundamental/Title and Tax/IP proposals below, it would sweep title, tax, IP, specific indemnities and payment covenants into an 18-month, AUD 4.8m, deductible-basket regime by default.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" default and replace with the opposite rule: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated; the Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity and covenant regimes are separate and unaffected.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket / de minimis / knowledge bar.
- **Analysis:** Reject outright. A title claim is a claim that we did not get what we paid for; capping it at 20% and time-barring it at 18 months is incompatible with the deal. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
- **Push back:** Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime on playbook terms.

### 1.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature"
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Analysis:** "All Claims of any nature" on its face captures fraud. This is a non-negotiable carve-out for us. It also likely extends the non-reliance clause to specific indemnities and pre-contractual representations we are relying on (e.g. Bluefen revenue figures), which the ACL would in any event limit but we should not leave to argument.
- **Push back:** Express carve-out for fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct from every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause. Also carve specific indemnities and the Fundamental, Tax and IP regimes out of 12.8 / 20.5.

### 1.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2 – General disclosure
- **Seller:** whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Analysis:** Para 1.1 is a blanket data-room disclosure; para 1.2 is a public-register disclosure. Combined with clause 8.3 (below), the effect is that anything that *could* have been found anywhere is deemed disclosed against every warranty. Note para 1.4 also purports that nothing in the letter admits that any consent, payment or notification is "legally required" – that is fine as a non-admission, but it must not be read as the Seller having no obligation to procure those things under the SPA conditions.
- **Push back:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Require disclosure to be specific, accurate and with sufficient particularity to allow a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Documents may be cross-referenced in a specific disclosure but the data room as a whole is not disclosed.

### 1.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Analysis:** This is the broadest form of knowledge bar: actual *and* constructive knowledge, imputed from advisers, and extended to anything "discoverable". It would effectively convert our due diligence into a defence for the Seller. It also has no carve-out for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Push back:** Delete clause 8.3 in its entirety. If the Seller insists on any knowledge concept, it should run the other way: seller warranties qualified by "so far as the Seller is aware" only where expressly stated, defined by reference to named individuals after due enquiry.

### 1.8 Clause 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent (the single largest commercial exposure)
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient.
- **Facts from Disclosure Letter para 2:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of the business). Clause 11.2 is a change-control consent and 11.3 attaches conditions. The Seller **confirms no final written consent and no evidence of conditions satisfied** as at 22 September 2026. The Seller's cover note says the matter "is addressed" – it is not.
- **Analysis:** A consent that is delivered but has unsatisfied conditions can lapse or be revoked. On a 30%-revenue customer this is a condition-precedent-grade issue. Note the data room cut-off is 22 September 2026 and today is 5 November 2026 – the factual position may have moved; we should refresh rather than assume.
- **Push back:** Make it a Completion condition that (a) an unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 is obtained in agreed form, and (b) the Seller delivers evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that each 11.3 condition is satisfied or waived by Bluefen. Seller obligation to be "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with a Buyer right to terminate if not satisfied by the long-stop date. Ask for a current status update on Bluefen.

### 1.9 Clause 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval (not given).
- **Facts (DL para 3):** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-control cl 8.1 and discharge cl 9.2; not repaid; no final discharge of security. Note the amount is "approximately" and as at 22 September – we need a current payout letter.
- **Analysis:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. If we complete with the facility outstanding and security in place, we have paid full price for an encumbered company and are relying on the Seller to procure a release later. The change-of-control clause 8.1 may also give Riverlark a default/acceleration right on Completion.
- **Push back:** Obtain a Riverlark payout letter dated within a few days of Completion; repayment direct from Completion funds to Riverlark per the funds flow; executed deeds of release and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion (or at minimum an irrevocable release undertaking from Riverlark conditional only on receipt of the payout amount – and that alternative needs Amelia Frost sign-off before we concede it).

### 1.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Facts (DL para 5):** bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; they do not appear in the funds flow; the Seller does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- **Analysis:** These bonuses are triggered *by* Completion and are payable by the Company, so absent a mechanism, they are a post-Completion cost borne by us. "A matter for the Seller" is only true if the SPA actually makes it so. On-costs (super at the applicable SG rate, NSW payroll tax, possibly leave loading) could add a meaningful percentage on top of AUD 420k; we should not estimate a figure without verifying who the recipients are and the terms.
- **Push back:** Either (a) a specific funds-flow line item deducting AUD 420,000 plus all employer on-costs from the price / treated as Debt, or (b) a Seller covenant and indemnity to fund the gross amount. Request the bonus letters and a calculation of on-costs.

### 1.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Facts (DL para 4):** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Analysis:** The real risk is not the AUD 180k – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at Completion if any fee is unpaid. An indemnity for "the payment" does not cover loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, or re-development cost. We should not take the AUD 180k as established either way – the Seller itself says DD-010 is not bank verification.
- **Push back:** (a) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, or a Seller obligation to procure them; (b) broaden cl 11.1 to an indemnity for all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to the Ironquay Project Materials or any Ironquay claim, uncapped by the general regime; (c) retain the SOW3 cure mechanic as the primary route.

### 1.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Facts (DL para 6):** download link sent to an unintended external email; possibly ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; notification question unresolved.
- **Analysis:** We should neither accept "not material" nor assert that there is a notifiable data breach. The playbook position is deliberately neutral. What matters is that the question is answered before Completion and that we are protected if it turns out badly. The 22 September cut-off is now six weeks old – there should be a further update.
- **Push back:** Seller covenant to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation (including access logs for the link), and provide updates pre-Completion; a specific warranty on the facts of the incident; a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (including any regulatory response or notification costs if it is ultimately determined to be required) outside the general cap/basket. Do not put a number on it.

### 1.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Facts (DL para 8):** three related renewals of AUD 110k each in DD-008 / DD-011; disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Analysis:** We agree with the playbook that this is not automatically a price deduction. But the Seller's "ordinary course" label is an assertion, and the disclosure itself does not support it. The point to resolve is whether any amount was accrued or payable pre-Completion (in which case it belongs in the completion accounts / working capital or Debt), and whether the renewals lock the Company in.
- **Push back:** Request the renewal documents and terms (start date, term, termination rights, amounts accrued pre-Completion). Position: treat as a completion-accounts / working capital item pending that review, with the Buyer reserving its position.

### 1.14 Tax / IP warranties
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime".
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; keep categories separate.
- **Push back:** Do not accept that Tax/IP are "settled". State expressly that Tax and IP regimes are reserved and will be addressed separately, outside the general cap/basket/time-limit and outside the clause 13 default rule. We are not asking for unlimited liability at this stage; we are refusing to let them collapse into the 20%/18-month regime by default.

### 1.15 Title evidence
- **Seller:** title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Playbook:** require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
- **Facts (DL para 10):** the Seller concedes DD-012 is merely "the source relied on" and does not state that the Buyer has verified it.
- **Push back:** Pre-Completion deliverables: current ASIC extracts for the Company and the Seller, PPSR searches against the Company (and the shares), evidence that Riverlark's security over the shares (if any) is released, Seller board/shareholder approvals, and a copy of the register together with the underlying share certificates / transfer history. Fundamental title warranties on playbook terms.

### 1.16 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Neither is characterised by the Seller as requiring consent to the share sale, and nothing in the Disclosure Letter contradicts that. These do not appear to be playbook departures, but we should confirm by reading the clauses ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation: (a) that the lease notification is only a notification and is given on time; (b) that Mossvale's assignment restriction has no change-of-control limb. Request a Seller covenant to give the DD-007 notification before or at Completion.

---

## 2. Structural observations

1. **The draft is internally coordinated to produce one regime.** Clause 13's "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated", the Fundamental/Title proposal, the "all Claims of any nature" wording in 9.3/12.8/20.5 and the "Tax/IP settled under the general regime" line together collapse every category into 20% / AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible / 18 months / buyer-knowledge-barred. Each must be rejected individually, but the response should also state the structural point: separate regimes for General, Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenants, with no default cross-application.

2. **The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the cover note.** The Letter concedes: no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark release, no Ironquay receipt/assignment, bonuses not in funds flow, incident unresolved, Sandbar unassessed, title based on an internal register. The cover note describes each of these as "addressed", "adequate", "not material" or "ordinary course". We should quote the Letter back to the Seller.

3. **Facts are stale.** Data room cut-off 22 September 2026; today is 5 November 2026. Before responding on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006, request a bring-down of the factual position. Treat anything new from the Seller as an assertion until documented.

4. **No authority to move.** Both of the Seller's headline numbers coincide with our fallbacks. We have no written authority from Amelia Frost on either, and this memo does not recommend seeking it at this stage – the Seller has given no concession on any other point that would justify spending those fallbacks.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "Final / agreed / market" framing | Positions settled and final | Reject; treat as opening draft; ask for basis of "settled" claim |
| 1 | General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Hold 25% / AUD 6.0m; no fallback without Amelia Frost authority |
| 2 | Thresholds (12.2) | AUD 25k / AUD 250k / excess-only | AUD 5k / AUD 50k / first-dollar |
| 3 | Claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months + default applies to all Claims | 24 months; delete default; limitations apply only where expressly stated |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |
| 5 | Limitations/non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | All Claims of any nature | Carve out fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct; carve out specific indemnities and separate regimes |
| 6 | Disclosure (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Actual/constructive/adviser/discoverable knowledge bar | Delete entirely |
| 8 | Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | Completion condition: unconditional consent + evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied; refresh status |
| 9 | Riverlark (2/7) | Post-Completion release | Current payout letter; repay from Completion funds; releases at Completion (post-Completion alternative only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval) |
| 10 | Bonuses (DD-005) | Not itemised; "Seller matter" | Specific line item or Seller-funded, grossed up for on-costs; request bonus letters |
| 11 | Ironquay (11.1) | SOW3 payment only | Pre-Completion payment evidence + confirmatory assignment; broaden indemnity to title defects/claims; keep SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified |
| 12 | DD-006 incident (4.6/Sch 6) | Not material | Preserve logs; complete investigation; updates; specific warranty and indemnity; no characterisation or number either way |
| 13 | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary course | Assess on documents; no automatic Debt/price deduction; reserve position |
| 14 | Tax / IP | Settled under general regime | OPEN; separate regimes; no default roll-up |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent evidence: ASIC, PPSR, approvals, certificates; fundamental warranties |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only / no consent | Verify ourselves; covenant to give DD-007 notice |

**Immediate actions:** (1) send a mark-up rejecting the general-regime roll-up and the "final" framing; (2) issue a factual bring-down request on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-005 on-costs, DD-006 and Sandbar; (3) commission independent title and PPSR searches; (4) confirm to the deal team that no fallback positions are to be offered without documented authority from Amelia Frost.

We have no record of any principal-level agreement on these terms, and nothing from Amelia Frost authorising any fallback. Note in particular that the Seller's cap (20% / AUD 4.8m) and claims period (18 months) happen to match exactly our *conditional* fallbacks – that is not a coincidence we should reward. A number matching a fallback does not clear it; the fallback is only usable with prior written authority identifying the draft, and none exists. **Recommendation: respond on the basis that the Seller's draft is an opening position, and ask the Seller to identify the basis for the "settled at principal level" statement.**

The Disclosure Letter's own para 11 ("No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included") actually contradicts the cover note's claim that positions are agreed – worth pointing out.

## 1. Clause-by-clause departures

### 1.1 Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 opening; 20% is fallback-only with Amelia Frost written approval (not given).
- **Push back:** Hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal that 20% is acceptable. If the deal team wants to move, that is a decision for Amelia Frost to document first.

### 1.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Analysis:** Three separate degradations – the de minimis is 5x ours, the basket 5x ours, and the basket is converted from a tipping basket to a deductible. On a AUD 24m SaaS target, a AUD 25k de minimis would exclude a large proportion of realistic operational claims (e.g. individual customer/supplier issues, employee entitlement errors). The "1% basket is market" assertion in the preamble is just an assertion.
- **Push back:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket. This is a material economic point, not drafting.

### 1.3 Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and the "all Claims" catch-all
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is fallback-only with Amelia Frost approval (not given). Fundamental/Title at least six years; Tax/IP open and separate.
- **Analysis:** The 18 months is the same fallback-matching tactic as the cap. The second sentence is the more dangerous one: it is a **hidden general-regime override**. Combined with the Seller's Fundamental/Title and Tax/IP proposals below, it would sweep title, tax, IP, specific indemnities and payment covenants into an 18-month, AUD 4.8m, deductible-basket regime by default.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" default and replace with the opposite rule: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated; the Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity and covenant regimes are separate and unaffected.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket / de minimis / knowledge bar.
- **Analysis:** Reject outright. A title claim is a claim that we did not get what we paid for; capping it at 20% and time-barring it at 18 months is incompatible with the deal. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
- **Push back:** Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime on playbook terms.

### 1.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature"
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Analysis:** "All Claims of any nature" on its face captures fraud. This is a non-negotiable carve-out for us. It also likely extends the non-reliance clause to specific indemnities and pre-contractual representations we are relying on (e.g. Bluefen revenue figures), which the ACL would in any event limit but we should not leave to argument.
- **Push back:** Express carve-out for fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct from every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause. Also carve specific indemnities and the Fundamental, Tax and IP regimes out of 12.8 / 20.5.

### 1.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2 – General disclosure
- **Seller:** whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Analysis:** Para 1.1 is a blanket data-room disclosure; para 1.2 is a public-register disclosure. Combined with clause 8.3 (below), the effect is that anything that *could* have been found anywhere is deemed disclosed against every warranty. Note para 1.4 also purports that nothing in the letter admits that any consent, payment or notification is "legally required" – that is fine as a non-admission, but it must not be read as the Seller having no obligation to procure those things under the SPA conditions.
- **Push back:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Require disclosure to be specific, accurate and with sufficient particularity to allow a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Documents may be cross-referenced in a specific disclosure but the data room as a whole is not disclosed.

### 1.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Analysis:** This is the broadest form of knowledge bar: actual *and* constructive knowledge, imputed from advisers, and extended to anything "discoverable". It would effectively convert our due diligence into a defence for the Seller. It also has no carve-out for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Push back:** Delete clause 8.3 in its entirety. If the Seller insists on any knowledge concept, it should run the other way: seller warranties qualified by "so far as the Seller is aware" only where expressly stated, defined by reference to named individuals after due enquiry.

### 1.8 Clause 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent (the single largest commercial exposure)
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient.
- **Facts from Disclosure Letter para 2:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of the business). Clause 11.2 is a change-control consent and 11.3 attaches conditions. The Seller **confirms no final written consent and no evidence of conditions satisfied** as at 22 September 2026. The Seller's cover note says the matter "is addressed" – it is not.
- **Analysis:** A consent that is delivered but has unsatisfied conditions can lapse or be revoked. On a 30%-revenue customer this is a condition-precedent-grade issue. Note the data room cut-off is 22 September 2026 and today is 5 November 2026 – the factual position may have moved; we should refresh rather than assume.
- **Push back:** Make it a Completion condition that (a) an unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 is obtained in agreed form, and (b) the Seller delivers evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that each 11.3 condition is satisfied or waived by Bluefen. Seller obligation to be "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with a Buyer right to terminate if not satisfied by the long-stop date. Ask for a current status update on Bluefen.

### 1.9 Clause 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval (not given).
- **Facts (DL para 3):** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-control cl 8.1 and discharge cl 9.2; not repaid; no final discharge of security. Note the amount is "approximately" and as at 22 September – we need a current payout letter.
- **Analysis:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. If we complete with the facility outstanding and security in place, we have paid full price for an encumbered company and are relying on the Seller to procure a release later. The change-of-control clause 8.1 may also give Riverlark a default/acceleration right on Completion.
- **Push back:** Obtain a Riverlark payout letter dated within a few days of Completion; repayment direct from Completion funds to Riverlark per the funds flow; executed deeds of release and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion (or at minimum an irrevocable release undertaking from Riverlark conditional only on receipt of the payout amount – and that alternative needs Amelia Frost sign-off before we concede it).

### 1.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Facts (DL para 5):** bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; they do not appear in the funds flow; the Seller does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- **Analysis:** These bonuses are triggered *by* Completion and are payable by the Company, so absent a mechanism, they are a post-Completion cost borne by us. "A matter for the Seller" is only true if the SPA actually makes it so. On-costs (super at the applicable SG rate, NSW payroll tax, possibly leave loading) could add a meaningful percentage on top of AUD 420k; we should not estimate a figure without verifying who the recipients are and the terms.
- **Push back:** Either (a) a specific funds-flow line item deducting AUD 420,000 plus all employer on-costs from the price / treated as Debt, or (b) a Seller covenant and indemnity to fund the gross amount. Request the bonus letters and a calculation of on-costs.

### 1.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Facts (DL para 4):** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Analysis:** The real risk is not the AUD 180k – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at Completion if any fee is unpaid. An indemnity for "the payment" does not cover loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, or re-development cost. We should not take the AUD 180k as established either way – the Seller itself says DD-010 is not bank verification.
- **Push back:** (a) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, or a Seller obligation to procure them; (b) broaden cl 11.1 to an indemnity for all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to the Ironquay Project Materials or any Ironquay claim, uncapped by the general regime; (c) retain the SOW3 cure mechanic as the primary route.

### 1.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Facts (DL para 6):** download link sent to an unintended external email; possibly ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; notification question unresolved.
- **Analysis:** We should neither accept "not material" nor assert that there is a notifiable data breach. The playbook position is deliberately neutral. What matters is that the question is answered before Completion and that we are protected if it turns out badly. The 22 September cut-off is now six weeks old – there should be a further update.
- **Push back:** Seller covenant to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation (including access logs for the link), and provide updates pre-Completion; a specific warranty on the facts of the incident; a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (including any regulatory response or notification costs if it is ultimately determined to be required) outside the general cap/basket. Do not put a number on it.

### 1.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Facts (DL para 8):** three related renewals of AUD 110k each in DD-008 / DD-011; disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Analysis:** We agree with the playbook that this is not automatically a price deduction. But the Seller's "ordinary course" label is an assertion, and the disclosure itself does not support it. The point to resolve is whether any amount was accrued or payable pre-Completion (in which case it belongs in the completion accounts / working capital or Debt), and whether the renewals lock the Company in.
- **Push back:** Request the renewal documents and terms (start date, term, termination rights, amounts accrued pre-Completion). Position: treat as a completion-accounts / working capital item pending that review, with the Buyer reserving its position.

### 1.14 Tax / IP warranties
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime".
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; keep categories separate.
- **Push back:** Do not accept that Tax/IP are "settled". State expressly that Tax and IP regimes are reserved and will be addressed separately, outside the general cap/basket/time-limit and outside the clause 13 default rule. We are not asking for unlimited liability at this stage; we are refusing to let them collapse into the 20%/18-month regime by default.

### 1.15 Title evidence
- **Seller:** title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Playbook:** require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
- **Facts (DL para 10):** the Seller concedes DD-012 is merely "the source relied on" and does not state that the Buyer has verified it.
- **Push back:** Pre-Completion deliverables: current ASIC extracts for the Company and the Seller, PPSR searches against the Company (and the shares), evidence that Riverlark's security over the shares (if any) is released, Seller board/shareholder approvals, and a copy of the register together with the underlying share certificates / transfer history. Fundamental title warranties on playbook terms.

### 1.16 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Neither is characterised by the Seller as requiring consent to the share sale, and nothing in the Disclosure Letter contradicts that. These do not appear to be playbook departures, but we should confirm by reading the clauses ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation: (a) that the lease notification is only a notification and is given on time; (b) that Mossvale's assignment restriction has no change-of-control limb. Request a Seller covenant to give the DD-007 notification before or at Completion.

## 2. Structural observations

1. **The draft is internally coordinated to produce one regime.** Clause 13's "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated", the Fundamental/Title proposal, the "all Claims of any nature" wording in 9.3/12.8/20.5 and the "Tax/IP settled under the general regime" line together collapse every category into 20% / AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible / 18 months / buyer-knowledge-barred. Each must be rejected individually, but the response should also state the structural point: separate regimes for General, Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenants, with no default cross-application.

2. **The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the cover note.** The Letter concedes: no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark release, no Ironquay receipt/assignment, bonuses not in funds flow, incident unresolved, Sandbar unassessed, title based on an internal register. The cover note describes each of these as "addressed", "adequate", "not material" or "ordinary course". We should quote the Letter back to the Seller.

3. **Facts are stale.** Data room cut-off 22 September 2026; today is 5 November 2026. Before responding on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006, request a bring-down of the factual position. Treat anything new from the Seller as an assertion until documented.

4. **No authority to move.** Both of the Seller's headline numbers coincide with our fallbacks. We have no written authority from Amelia Frost on either, and this memo does not recommend seeking it at this stage – the Seller has given no concession on any other point that would justify spending those fallbacks.
